description: Add phase PH-4 "Cross-cutting hardening & release" and bind slices SL-016 through SL-019 to it. This introduces structure absent from every v1 artifact, so it is recorded as a typed scope change before the mutation it authorizes. Authorized by DEC-029. No requirement, acceptance criterion or work item changes scope as a result; the four slices already existed in the roadmap ladder and had already shipped. The change is representational only. Re-applied on the 2.4.0 re-population of 2026-07-23.

Extend the v1 deployment target from on-prem-only to AWS cloud-hosted UAT + production. The charter and ADR-0013/CON-001/CON-003/INV-003 fixed a self-contained on-prem target; this change adds a cloud target hosted on AWS EC2 + Docker Compose, with Keycloak folded onto SQL Server, MinIO replaced by S3, and the container set consolidated. Introduces phase PH-5 and slices SL-020..SL-027, four Proposed ADRs (0034-0037), two defects (DEF-014/015), eleven acceptance criteria (AC-075..AC-085), risk rows, and open questions. Authorized by DEC-030. No PH-1..PH-4 requirement, AC, or work item changes scope; the on-prem P1-P19 ladder is unaffected and its artefacts are untouched. Recorded before the mutations it authorizes.

REFINES ADR-0038's persistence decision, discovered by reading the domain BEFORE writing code. ADR-0038 says the invite writes 'Keycloak plus a lightweight invite record ONLY — it does NOT create the CommitteeMember row', to avoid a distributed write whose failure leaves an orphan that DEF-029 makes permanent, and to keep ProvisionCurrentUser (ADR-0004) the single creation path. THE DOMAIN ALREADY MODELS THIS FEATURE and models it better. MembershipStatus.Invited exists (value 1) and its own comment reads 'Invited is reserved for admin PRE-REGISTRATION AHEAD OF FIRST LOGIN — P4 produces Active/Disabled; the directory renders all three'. CommitteeMember.SyncFromClaims already implements the other half: 'A login on a pre-registered Invited record flips it to Active', with an explicit `activating` flag so that transition is audited EVEN WHEN name, email and role are unchanged. So the invite path the ADR proposed to build from scratch is already half-built, and a second parallel concept would duplicate a modelled one. THE ADR'S OBJECTION DOES NOT APPLY HERE: its worry was reconciling a row whose Keycloak `sub` is unknown at creation — exactly why DEC-033 rejected pre-seeding 26 members — but an app-driven invite CREATES the Keycloak user and receives its id in the response, so the sub is known and there is nothing to reconcile. The residual failure mode also inverts and becomes benign: if the Keycloak create succeeds and the local insert fails, what is left over is a Keycloak user with NO member row, which the existing JIT path provisions on first login. Nothing permanent is damaged, because the permanent-orphan risk lives in the member row and no member row was written. CHANGE: the invite creates a CommitteeMember at Status=Invited carrying the KeycloakUserId returned by Keycloak; first login flips it to Active through the existing SyncFromClaims path, unchanged. The roster (FR-158 / DEF-038) is then ONE query over members rather than a union with a second table, and no new entity, table or migration is introduced. ADR-0038's other decisions — one client behind an IIdentityProvider port, minimum realm-management scope, file-backed secret, temp password shown once, ACMP-side guest expiry, forced sign-out, and the four guards — are unaffected.

ADR-0038 SUPERSEDES ONE CLAUSE OF ADR-0015, AND NEITHER ROW SAID SO UNTIL NOW. Found on 2026-08-11 while wiring the invite panel: an existing frontend test was named 'UserDetail (read-only, no invite per ADR-0015)' and asserted `queryByText(/invit/i)` was absent. That test was not stale — IT WAS FAITHFULLY ENCODING A REAL DECISION. ADR-0015 §Q3 states: 'User provisioning is manual via the self-hosted Keycloak admin console (Q3 decision). ACMP does NOT integrate the Keycloak Admin API in v1, so the Membership module / P4 is unaffected — it still just consumes identity and JIT-provisions a local profile on first login.' ADR-0038 reverses exactly that: it integrates the Keycloak Admin API and gives the Membership module an outbound write. ADR-0038 was written without citing ADR-0015 at all, so an Approved ADR was contradicted silently — the precise drift AGENTS.md's 'ADRs are FINAL; supersede via a new ADR row' exists to prevent, and it was caught by a TEST rather than by any gate, because the citation lived in a describe-block name and no mechanical check reads those. SCOPE OF THE SUPERSESSION, deliberately narrow: ONLY the Q3 'manual provisioning / no Admin API in v1' clause is overtaken. Everything else in ADR-0015 stands unchanged and is in fact reinforced by ADR-0038 — Keycloak stays self-hosted with an ACMP-owned realm, there is still NO self-registration, identity is still federated with roles arriving as claims, and the stack still has zero external runtime services (the Admin API call is to ACMP's OWN bundled Keycloak, not to anything outside the deployment). ADR-0015 is therefore NOT marked superseded as a whole, because it is not: doing so would discard a self-hosting decision that remains load-bearing. WHY THE REVERSAL IS COHERENT WITH ADR-0015's OWN REASONING: ADR-0015 lists 'ACMP now OWNS IdP operations' as its accepted trade-off. Manual console provisioning was the v1 expression of that ownership; DEC-038 is the operator deciding to exercise the same ownership through the product instead of through the console, which is a change of mechanism rather than of principle. The test now asserts the invite section IS present and names this supersession in place, so the next reader meets the reasoning rather than an assertion that silently flipped.

ADR-0039'S ENFORCEMENT POINT MOVED FROM JwtBearerEvents.OnTokenValidated TO A SCHEME-AGNOSTIC MIDDLEWARE, AND THE REASON IS EVIDENCE RATHER THAN TASTE. ADR-0039 was approved on 2026-08-12 specifying the check run 'in JwtBearerEvents.OnTokenValidated — the seam that already runs per request and already resolves DI'. It was implemented there first and it WORKED; the build was green. The problem surfaced while writing the test that proves it. THE API INTEGRATION HOST DOES NOT AUTHENTICATE WITH JWT AT ALL. tests/Acmp.Api.Tests/TestAuthHandler.cs is a separate AuthenticationHandler registered under its own 'Test' scheme, building the principal from X-Test-Roles / X-Test-Sub headers with no token, no signature and no issuer. A JwtBearer event therefore CANNOT RUN IN ANY API TEST, which means the approved seam could only ever have been proven by unit-testing IPrincipalRevalidator in isolation — i.e. by asserting that a collaborator returns the right verdict, never that a REQUEST is refused. That is exactly the 'a handler was called' evidence AV-134 refused for this very AC, and AC-090's bar is explicit: 'proven by asserting the user's SUBSEQUENT REQUEST no longer exercises the removed role, not merely that a logout call was issued'. CHANGE: the check is a PrincipalRevalidationMiddleware registered between UseAuthentication and UseAuthorization. Everything else in ADR-0039 is untouched — the same IPrincipalRevalidator contract, the same Membership-owned implementation, the same local-read-not-introspection decision, the same fail-closed verdicts, the same placement before any policy or handler sees the principal. WHY THE NEW SEAM IS STRICTLY BETTER, not merely more testable: it is scheme-agnostic, so it covers every authenticated request however the principal was established, where the JwtBearer hook covered only one scheme and would have silently exempted any future one. The approved seam is SUBSUMED rather than abandoned. WHAT IT COST TO FIND: nothing, because it was found by writing the test rather than after shipping — but it is worth recording that an approved ADR named an implementation detail that could not be evidenced, and the ADR review did not catch it. The lesson generalises: when an ADR names a specific seam, check that the test harness can reach it BEFORE approving. ALSO CHANGED, minimally: TestAuthHandler gained an optional X-Test-Iat header so a test can say 'this token was issued before the change'. Without it the staleness comparison has no input and the refusal cannot be forced through the pipeline at all.

description: THE /session TOPIC CARD OMITS THE DESIGN'S ALT-LANGUAGE TITLE, BECAUSE NO SUCH DATA HAS EVER EXISTED. Recorded before the build it authorizes, not after review. DEC-037 fixes the /session content by reference to 'ACMP Navigation & IA.dc.html' lines 304-347, and line 320 renders a second title in the OTHER language beneath the primary one, with dir flipped. INV-014 requires matching that reference exactly, so dropping a line is a deliberate divergence rather than a detail. WHAT THE DOMAIN ACTUALLY HAS: Topic carries a single `Title` string and a single `Description`. There is no LocalizedString type anywhere in the codebase and no *_Ar column on Topic - nor is there a capture point for one, at intake, triage, preparation or edit. The reference therefore asks for a field the system has never held, which makes this a DATA gap the design could not see rather than a rendering choice. WHY THE CODE IS RIGHT AND THE REFERENCE IS AHEAD OF IT: satisfying line 320 honestly means a migration, a second title field on the submit and the edit forms, bilingual validation, and a backfill decision for every topic already in the system - a bilingual-content feature in its own right, larger than the whole /session shell and orthogonal to AC-092, which is about expiry being real and server-enforced. Rendering an empty element, or duplicating the same title twice under a flipped direction, would be worse than omitting it: both would state to a reader that a translation exists. SCOPE, deliberately narrow: ONLY the alt-title line is dropped. Everything else on the topic card is built as drawn and maps cleanly - the TOP key to Topic.Key, the heading to Topic.Title, the summary block to Topic.Description - and every other element of the GUEST/PRESENTER SHELL (banner, slot card, materials list) is built in full. If bilingual topic titles are later wanted, they get their own FR and /session gains the line for free.
